text:
maya: quick sync: proposing we unify metrics_events_raw + metrics_events_normalized into a single table metric_events_v2 to avoid repeated ETL and mismatched rows. rationale: duplication causes stale joins and doubles storage/indexing costs. sketch PR: https://github.com/redwood/analytics/pull/990

dmitri: big +1 for storage savings, but concerns about query performance. normalized table had denormalized columns for hot queries (route_name, team_id). How do we keep fast aggregator queries?

maya: plan is polymorphic storage: keep core columns (id, route_id, metric_name, ts, value) and a compressed attrs jsonb (attrs_compressed bytea) plus a small set of denorm columns we expect in 95% of queries (route_name, team_id, customer_tier). Also add tags_hash column for equality filters to enable index-only lookups.

carla: what about existing dashboards that do WHERE attrs->>'env' = 'prod' or use attrs->'labels' ? We need read compatibility layer.

ben: propose compatibility view metric_events_compat that exposes attrs as jsonb with a lazy-decompress function so reads work unchanged. Writers will dual-write to new table and old normalized copy for a grace period. views avoid breaking saved queries.

maya: migration steps (high-level):
1) create metric_events_v2 table with columns: id UUID, route_id, metric_name text, ts timestamptz, value double precision, route_name text, team_id uuid, customer_tier text, tags_hash bigint, attrs_compressed bytea, attrs_uncompressed jsonb GENERATED ALWAYS AS (pgp_sym_decrypt(attrs_compressed, current_setting('app.enc_key')) ) STORED; -- if we can get compressed computed col support; otherwise use view
2) add indexes concurrently on (route_id, metric_name, ts) and on tags_hash
3) update ingestion service to dual-write to v2 and normalized target for 2 weeks
4) run backfill for last 90 days for low-write tenants first; emit progress metrics
5) switch Console read path to prefer v2 via feature flag per-tenant
6) after validation and 30d stable, retire normalized table and alias name to metric_events

dmitri: careful on computed compressed/uncompressed approach; Postgres doesn't like heavy crypto functions in generated columns. If we can't have stored decompression, I'd prefer storing attrs_compressed and a simple attrs_decomp view that decompresses on demand. That keeps table smaller and avoids CPU on writes.

carla: index design: for common filters we should support a GIN on attrs_uncompressed (jsonb_path_ops) but that defeats compression. Alternative: maintain tags_hash for frequently-filtered tag sets (e.g., env, region). We'll include a small column set route_name/team_id that covers most group-bys.

ben: sample SQL to make tags_hash index concurrently:
```sql
ALTER TABLE metric_events_v2 ADD COLUMN tags_hash bigint;
UPDATE metric_events_v2 SET tags_hash = (hashtext((attrs_uncompressed->> 'env') || '|' || (attrs_uncompressed->> 'region')) ) WHERE tags_hash IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_metric_events_v2_tags_hash ON metric_events_v2 (tags_hash, ts DESC);
```
Note: hashtext is illustrative; we'll use xxhash or pg_strhash extension for stable 64-bit.

maya: backfill planner: per-tenant worker that reads from normalized table and writes a compact row into v2. Safety: skip tenants with >10000 events/day, throttle to 1000 inserts/sec, and use MVCC-friendly chunking by id range. Progress written to /infra/backfills/metrics_v2/<tenant>.json and metrics prometheus.backfill.metrics_v2.progress.

carla: Console needs to show a migration status at tenant-level: fields migrated_count, percent_complete, last_backfill_ts, and fallback_toggle. Also add audit log entry when toggle flipped. UX: a single line in Settings -> Data: "Use unified metrics storage (beta) [On/Off]" with tooltip about compatibility view.

ben: monitoring/QA: nightly compare job that executes a small canonical query set (200 saved charts sample) against normalized table vs metric_events_v2 via the compatibility view. Acceptance: counts +/- 0.3% and aggregates within tolerance; p95 latency not worse than 1.5x baseline for those sample queries. We'll also compute index/not-index plan differences and capture explains for outliers.
dmitri: backfill cost: estimate 8TB scanned, assume 50MB/s effective throughput per worker -> ~2 days with 4 workers. But I want to ensure backfill respects maintenance windows on prod clusters. We'll schedule initial backfill in off-peak window and do a pilot on canary cluster.

maya: rollout phases: dev -> staging -> canary (1 tenant) -> canary (10 tenants) -> 20% orgs -> 100%. Abort if nightly compare fails 2 days in a row, if dashboard owners report >0.5% mismatches for critical dashboards, or if index bloat >20% on monitored nodes. Also abort if write latency p99 increases by >30ms.

carla: QA note: many saved queries rely on implicit casting and exploded jsonb fields. We'll add a lint pass in the Console that flags queries referencing attrs->> or jsonb_extract on old table and recommend using compatibility view or new denorm columns.

ben: deployment hooks: ingestion change guarded by feature flag. We'll implement a consumer-side idempotency token to avoid double inserts when retries occur during dual-write.

kb-bot: CI: PR #990 passed unit+integration tests. Canary deploy scheduled: 2026-04-05T03:00Z.

maya: action items: dmitri to prototype tags_hash and pg extension for fast hashing, ben to land backfill runner and prometheus metrics, carla to mock Console toggle and lint warnings, and I'll update PR with abort criteria and run pilot on canary next week. We'll share first-nightly compare results here.
